title: gmellon: headless gnome-keyring unlock CLI
description: Every unlock door on this SSH-only machine is shut: gcr-prompter needs X/Wayland; 'gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock' never forwards to a running (systemd socket-activated) daemon; pam_gnome_keyring is not installed and only fires on password logins; secret-tool deliberately has no unlock command; the Secret Service Unlock() call is prompt-gated. The daemon's private control protocol (OP_UNLOCK/OP_CHANGE on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/keyring/control) is the one interface that accepts a password from any client of ours — pam_gnome_keyring speaks it, gmellon is its shell-native sibling. Full spec in README.md (readme-driven development: README is the source of truth).
acceptance_criteria: gmellon unlock and gmellon change work against a real throwaway daemon (harness-verified), with TTY/stdin-only password input, --allow-create guard against unlock-or-create landmine, spec exit codes, and README-matching --help.

title: Compose CLI configuration with Firmament
description: Adopt the local Firmament checkout at ../firmament (~/src/firmament), our figment2 fork, for gmellon's one-shot non-secret configuration. Introduce a config domain that keeps invocation concerns (selected subcommand and password source) separate from composable settings. Derive clap Parser, serde Serialize/Deserialize, and bon Builder on the appropriate configuration input type, using Firmament's Serialized and Env providers. Precedence must be CLI > GMELLON_-prefixed environment > application defaults. Feed resolved control/data path settings into later local-store and command wiring rather than reading process environment throughout the application. Passwords and other secret values must never enter Firmament, environment configuration, files, provenance, or Debug output. Use the stable one-shot composition API; do not pull Firmament ops/state/live machinery into this CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo uses the local ../firmament dependency in a way that makes the eventual publish dependency decision explicit; clap parsing remains user-friendly and subcommand semantics are not treated as persisted configuration; a typed resolved config is composed with CLI > GMELLON_ env > defaults and validates required values after extraction; absent optional CLI values do not overwrite lower providers; XDG fallback inputs remain distinguishable from explicit gmellon overrides; no secret field is representable in the configuration model; deterministic tests cover each precedence level, absent-value behavior, invalid values, and separation of command/input-source from settings; README documents supported environment keys and local-checkout/publishing implications; rustfmt, clippy, rustdoc, and nextest pass.

title: Stage 2.5: secret input (TTY prompt + --stdin line)
description: Secret acquisition for unlock/change. TTY no-echo prompts via rpassword 7.5 on the controlling terminal (established local precedent: Atuin, tassle). Explicit --stdin path uses a small ordinary line-record reader behind an injectable BufRead seam, NOT rpassword's interactive editor, so piped control bytes (backspace, 0x7f, etc.) stay literal data. UTF-8 input contract: invalid UTF-8 errors rather than silently replacing; the control protocol itself stays raw-byte capable. Secret owns Zeroizing<String>, exposes as_bytes() only, no Debug/Clone/Display and no ownership escape. LF and CRLF terminate a line; EOF before newline errors; empty line passes through. Explicit bounded maximum input length so an untrusted pipe cannot drive unbounded allocation. TTY ENXIO (no controlling terminal) maps to an actionable error suggesting --stdin. Reusable two-prompt confirmation for Stage 4 change: single-shot mismatch error, both temporary values zeroized. Error values and messages never contain secret content.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests without a live TTY cover: LF termination, CRLF termination, empty line, invalid UTF-8 rejection, unterminated EOF error, at-limit acceptance, over-limit rejection, literal control bytes on the stdin path, matching and mismatching confirmation, ENXIO to actionable error mapping, and interop with control::sans_io encoding via Secret::as_bytes. rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, and nextest all clean. No public API leaks secret content through Debug/Display/Clone or by value.
notes:
Claimed for implementation. Architecture accepted from prior crate assessment: rpassword 7.5 for controlling-TTY no-echo prompts; explicit --stdin line-record reader behind injectable BufRead seam (pipes must not be interpreted by rpassword's interactive editor); UTF-8 input contract with error-not-replace; bounded input length; ENXIO -> actionable --stdin hint; reusable two-prompt confirmation.
Final shape: MAX_SECRET_BYTES = 64 KiB public const; read_stdin_line bounds buffering with reader.take(MAX+2).read_until so a never-terminating pipe cannot drive unbounded allocation; LF or CRLF terminate, lone CR is content, EOF-before-newline errors (empty pipe included), empty line yields empty secret, invalid UTF-8 errors via str::from_utf8 with no error path retaining bytes. prompt/prompt_confirmed wrap rpassword::prompt_password_with_config (controlling TTY); ENXIO from opening /dev/tty maps via classify_terminal_error to NoControllingTerminal suggesting --stdin. confirm_with(prompt, confirmation_prompt, impl FnMut(&str) -> Result<Secret, SecretError>) is the reusable Stage 4 core: single-shot mismatch, both temporaries zeroized on drop. Tests include the contrast test showing rpassword's configured reader edits piped control bytes while ours keeps them literal, plus sans_io encode/decode round-trips through Secret::as_bytes for ASCII and multibyte.
Post-review hardening commit 5cc5d988: stdin preallocates MAX_LINE_BYTES so secret prefixes cannot be abandoned by Vec reallocations; SecretError::Io retains only ErrorKind and numeric errno, discarding arbitrary reader text; TTY answers pass through the same 64 KiB limit while already inside Zeroizing<String>; public confirm_with was replaced by concrete read_stdin_confirmed and a private confirmation core; bounded-reader test now asserts logical consumption. README now scopes zeroization and rpassword terminal restoration as best-effort. Verified 54 nextest tests, 2 doctests, rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, and rustdoc -D warnings.
close_reason: Re-reviewed secret input now meets the bounded allocation, redacted error, shared size-limit, deep API, UTF-8, confirmation, and best-effort zeroization contracts.

title: Add synchronous control transport with async-ready seams
description: Build the synchronous Unix-socket adapter around the sans-I/O control codec. Keep framing and result parsing independent of I/O; keep path and peer validation usable with any AsFd socket; name the concrete adapter SyncClient so a future TokioClient can coexist without a generic async/sync trait. Each operation opens one daemon connection, validates the socket and peer UID, sends the credentials NUL followed by a zeroizing frame, reads the exact response under a timeout, and returns typed local/daemon outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: SyncClient exposes unlock and change; pure codec remains I/O-free; reusable Unix validation is not coupled to std::os::unix::net::UnixStream where AsFd suffices; fake Unix-server tests cover credential-byte ordering, UNLOCK and CHANGE exchange bytes, partial response delivery, missing/refused daemon, non-socket and symlink paths, peer validation, malformed/truncated responses, and bounded reads. No secret-bearing type implements Debug or leaks payloads. rustfmt, clippy, rustdoc, and nextest pass.
notes:
Implementation uses a sans-I/O protocol core plus an explicitly synchronous adapter. Future Tokio support should add a sibling adapter and reuse protocol + AsFd validation, not force async and sync through one trait.
Implemented as control::sans_io + Linux-only SyncClient + Metadata/AsFd Unix validation. Review corrections added an absolute response deadline resistant to drip-fed bytes, transport-level peer mismatch rejection before credential transmission, explicit Linux API gating, and proof that one client opens fresh connections. The timeout is documented as total response-read plus per-write, not an overall connect/exchange deadline. Standards review found no hard violations or code smells. Verified rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, and 28 nextest tests.
close_reason: Synchronous transport, async-ready seams, security validation, response deadline, typed errors, and complete fake-server coverage are implemented and reviewed.

title: Integrate real-daemon tests durably
description: Promote the useful control-only harness pieces into the maintained test workflow without making ordinary pure tests depend on an installed system daemon. Define an explicit real-daemon test entry point and tool-availability contract that cannot silently turn a requested integration run into a pass.
acceptance_criteria: The maintained test workflow exposes a clear opt-in for real-daemon tests; an explicit harness run fails clearly when required external tools are absent while ordinary test output makes non-running integration coverage visible; pure codec and fake-socket transport tests remain independent; relevant format, clippy, nextest, shell or static checks, and real-daemon harness tests pass through documented commands; failure artifacts remain redacted and useful.

title: Record the control-protocol behavior matrix
description: Use the reusable control-only harness and a minimal disposable probe, or reviewed product transport if available, to replace source-based assumptions with observations from the installed daemon. This ticket exercises only the private control socket; Secret Service observations belong to the optional broker child.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded reproducible probes cover missing login keyring plus UNLOCK, subsequent correct UNLOCK, wrong UNLOCK, CHANGE A-to-B followed by a daemon restart and verification that B succeeds while A is denied, missing-keyring CHANGE behavior, relevant empty-password behavior, and stopped or unresponsive daemon behavior needed by product tests; passwords and password-bearing frames never appear in output or retained logs; factual documentation is updated only where behavior was observed.

title: Provide a reusable harness lifecycle
description: Turn the reviewed smoke proof into a composable way to run a command or test inside an isolated daemon environment. Publish the child environment and selected paths through a clear contract while keeping daemon ownership, readiness, logs, and cleanup inside the harness.
acceptance_criteria: A caller can run a command inside a fresh harness instance and receives documented environment variables and exit semantics; startup and shutdown use bounded positive checks and exact owned PIDs or one dedicated process group; TERM is followed by bounded KILL only for remaining owned children and every child is reaped; signals and command failure preserve redacted logs; concurrent instances use no shared mutable paths, fixed sockets, or fixed PIDs; nesting behavior is either supported and tested or explicitly rejected.

title: Prove the isolated control-socket path
description: Prove one complete, safe path through a real throwaway daemon before designing a reusable interface. Launch one foreground daemon in a unique mode-0700 scratch HOME/XDG environment assembled explicitly for the child, poison both D-Bus addresses, sanitize inherited activation and session variables, and use a narrowly scoped disposable probe for the credential prelude and UNLOCK frame. Treat this as configuration/session isolation, not filesystem confinement.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded run observes initialization stdout EOF, child liveness, and the expected control socket type and ownership; fresh-store UNLOCK returns OK and a subsequent wrong password returns DENIED; known daemon paths remain beneath scratch and an external sentinel remains unchanged; no password or password-bearing frame is logged; normal and failure cleanup TERM/KILL/reaps only owned processes and retains useful failure evidence.
notes:
Implementation started from the approved epic frontier. Scope is limited to the isolated real-daemon smoke proof and its evidence; reusable lifecycle extraction remains in gmell-harness-lifecycle.
Implemented and reviewed. dev/harness/smoke.py now proves a real gnome-keyring-daemon 48.0 control-only path with an explicit empty-based environment, poisoned session/system buses, stdout-EOF/liveness/socket readiness, socket and SO_PEERCRED ownership, fresh UNLOCK OK, wrong-password DENIED, artifact/reported-path checks, pre/post-teardown sentinel checks, output redaction scans, reproducible failure retention, handled HUP/INT/TERM, and bounded exact-PID TERM/KILL/wait teardown. Evidence: doc/harness/smoke0.gpt6a.md. Verification: Python compile; normal and retained live smoke runs; deterministic failure, early-exit stdout, post-send response failure, SIGTERM and SIGHUP injections; cargo fmt; clippy -D warnings; nextest 28/28. GX final acceptance review passed. Non-blocking lifecycle caveat: harden the tiny first-signal-during-finally race when extracting the reusable runner in gmell-harness-lifecycle.
close_reason: Implemented, evidenced, and GX-reviewed: all smoke acceptance criteria pass against gnome-keyring-daemon 48.0; remaining signal-race hardening belongs to the now-unblocked lifecycle ticket.

title: Stage 3: unlock subcommand
description: Validate the control socket and connected peer ownership, connect to <control-dir>/control, write the required NUL credential byte, send UNLOCK, and parse the exact 8-byte result. TTY prompt via rpassword (default), single-line stdin (--stdin); passwords never via argv/flags or logs. --allow-create guard: refuse when the selected XDG data directory has no login.keyring, explaining the unlock-or-create behavior. Map daemon and local connection outcomes to documented exit codes.
acceptance_criteria: Fake-socket tests cover the credential prelude, peer/response validation, partial I/O, and bounded failure behavior. Harness integration test: fresh scratch daemon + unlock with correct password = exit 0; wrong password = exit 2; no login keyring + unlock refuses without --allow-create; with --allow-create creates and unlocks; stopped daemon = exit 4. No diagnostic output contains a password or password-bearing frame.
notes: Security requirement: hold password and password-bearing request data in zeroizing buffers and clear them immediately after the exchange; do not derive or emit Debug for secret-bearing types.

title: Stage 1: protocol codec with golden-byte tests
description: protocol.rs: pure functions, no I/O. u32 BE framing (self-inclusive length), op/result enums (INITIALIZE=0 UNLOCK=1 CHANGE=2 QUIT=3; OK=0 DENIED=1 FAILED=2 NO_DAEMON=3), length-prefixed strings without NUL. Locks the wire transcription from GNOME/gnome-keyring source before any socket opens.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests assert exact golden bytes incl. README's 'mellon' example (18-byte unlock frame, 8-byte OK response); roundtrip encode/decode tests; module has zero socket/file I/O.
notes:
Protocol reassessment: the golden request frame remains 18 bytes, but it is preceded on the stream by a separate NUL credential byte owned by the transport layer. Keep that byte out of the pure frame codec.
Implementation started with the agreed control-domain structure: src/lib.rs plus src/control/{mod.rs,protocol.rs}. Scope remains pure framing only; Unix credentials and socket I/O stay in the later transport slice.
Implemented and reviewed. Public codec now encodes and decodes UNLOCK/CHANGE requests over raw byte fields, decodes exact 8-byte results, uses zeroizing non-Debug request frames, and rejects malformed frames. Spec review's production-decoder and non-UTF8 gaps were fixed. Interior NUL and lengths >= 0x7fffffff remain rejected to match upstream egg_buffer_get_string/add_string behavior. Standards review found no violations or actionable smells. Verified rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, and 17 nextest tests.
close_reason: Pure protocol codec, golden vectors, production round trips, malformed-input coverage, and zeroizing request ownership are implemented and all checks pass.

title: Isolated GNOME Keyring integration harness
description: Build a reusable integration-test harness for gnome-keyring-daemon's private control socket without exposing the user's real keyring, session bus, system bus, or socket-activated daemon. The core path uses a fresh mode-0700 HOME/XDG tree, explicit unreachable bus addresses, a manually launched daemon, positive bounded readiness checks, owned-process teardown, and redacted evidence. An optional dbus-broker parity child explores Secret Service observations but is not part of the core blocking chain.
acceptance_criteria: The control-only harness has a documented environment and lifecycle contract; reproducible probes establish the required daemon behavior; maintained real-daemon tests have an explicit tool-availability policy; isolation and troubleshooting claims match collected evidence. The optional broker-parity child does not block core completion or product unlock work.
notes:
Assessment found this ticket needs a reviewed decomposition: isolated session bus, disabled host activation, explicit environment contract, readiness, exact-PID lifecycle, storage-isolation proof, behavioral probes, and durable test integration. Use doc/harness/prompt.md in a fresh Sol session; its Slice 0 proposes tickets before mutating this issue.
Sol assessment verified that session-bus failure is non-fatal for the control socket. dbus-broker-launch worked only through inherited socket activation with --scope system on this host; --scope user failed ENOMEDIUM and the launcher depends on the host journal socket. README and doc/harness/prompt.md now make broker support a later parity layer.
Supersedes the earlier decomposition note: after the completed assessment, Slice 0 is now authorized to create the namespaced harness tickets and implement only the control-only smoke test. The isolated bus is deferred to the broker-parity child.
2026-09-11 review: Converted this provisional task into an epic with six approved namespaced children. The core chain is smoke -> lifecycle -> behavior -> integration -> documentation. Broker parity branches after lifecycle and is explicitly non-blocking. The baseline is described precisely as configuration/session isolated rather than claiming filesystem-level hermetic confinement.

title: Stage 0: cargo scaffold + clap skeleton
description: cargo init; clap v4 derive with stub subcommands (unlock/change/status), --control-dir global flag; nextest wired; clippy+rustfmt clean. --help output should mirror the README usage spec.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build clean; gmellon --help prints all subcommands per README; clippy/fmt pass; nextest runs a trivial green test.
notes: Initialized Cargo binary with a domain-grouped CLI module, clap derive parser, global --control-dir, unlock/change/status stubs, and CLI definition tests. Verified cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and cargo nextest run.
close_reason: CLI scaffold and checks are implemented; 3 nextest tests pass.

title: Document and close the core harness
description: Reconcile the product README, harness guidance, and issue acceptance criteria with the implemented control-only harness and observed daemon behavior. Make the safe entry point and operational limits easy for later product work to understand.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation explains setup, invocation, required tools, readiness, process ownership, cleanup, parallelism, retained failure artifacts, and troubleshooting; isolation terminology states what the harness verifies without claiming filesystem-level confinement; a process diagram is included when it materially clarifies ownership; core tickets are closed only when their acceptance evidence exists, and remaining optional broker work is reported separately.

title: Package gmellon as a zimfw plugin
description: Provide a zimfw-compatible module entrypoint for lightweight shell integration. On load, select and validate the intended GNOME/GCR SSH agent socket and export SSH_AUTH_SOCK in the current shell. Default behavior is shell-local and idempotent. An explicit opt-in mode checks the systemd user manager environment and, only when SSH_AUTH_SOCK is absent there, publishes the selected value without replacing an existing value. Keep environment setup separate from unlocking: loading the module must not implicitly prompt for a password.
acceptance_criteria: The repository can be installed and loaded as a zimfw module using documented zmodule configuration; loading it repeatedly leaves the same valid SSH_AUTH_SOCK; socket selection has a documented explicit override and sensible GNOME/GCR discovery with actionable behavior when no socket exists; default mode never invokes systemctl and never prompts; opt-in systemd mode reads the user-manager environment, sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK only when missing, preserves any existing value exactly, and handles an unavailable user manager without corrupting the shell environment; zsh tests cover unset, already-set, missing-socket, repeated-load, systemd-missing, and systemd-already-present cases using test doubles rather than the real user manager.

title: Stage 5: status, redacted diagnostics, completions
description: status subcommand (offline only: control socket stat, keyring-dir inventory, alias resolution); redacted tracing that reports operation/result/lengths but never password-bearing frame bytes; clap_complete shell completions.
acceptance_criteria: gmellon status runs without touching the daemon and reports socket + keyring files without claiming live lock state; -v output contains useful operation metadata and no secret payload bytes; completions generated for at least zsh.

title: Stage 4: change subcommand (headless re-key)
description: OP_CHANGE frame (original, new) with old/new/confirm prompts. Uses harness to nail down and document behavior when no login keyring exists before shipping.
acceptance_criteria: Harness test: unlock A -> change A->B -> unlock B (0) -> unlock A (2 denied). Missing-keyring behavior documented in README behavior notes.

title: Assess optional private-broker parity
description: Explore a private dbus-broker parity topology for Secret Service observations without exposing the real user bus or permitting host service activation. Reproduce the known socket-activation composition before extending it, launch gnome-keyring-daemon manually, and keep this work independent of the required control-only harness.
acceptance_criteria: The experiment either demonstrates a private broker socket, minimal no-activation configuration, bounded readiness, a successful bus method call, manual daemon ownership of org.gnome.keyring and org.freedesktop.secrets, and clean owned-process shutdown, or documents that the required isolation boundary cannot be met; evidence identifies exact process and file-descriptor ownership plus host systemd and journal dependencies; dbus-daemon is used only as a diagnostic baseline; no unsafe fallback or real-bus contact is hidden; any Secret Service observations live with this ticket.

title: Stage 6 (stretch): lock via zbus, env exposure, shell-hook docs
description: Only if wanted: 'lock' via Secret Service D-Bus (zbus) for symmetry (locking is free, unlocking is prompt-gated — see secret-tool asymmetry); expose INITIALIZE env op; document zsh login-hook integration pattern.
acceptance_criteria: TBD when scoped; keep out of the critical path.
